query: In powder-vapourization (MoO3 + sulfur) CVD growth of MoS2, what do published experiments report about how sulfur boat temperature or sulfur boat position (sulfur supply) changes domain size, nucleation density, coverage or triangle vs truncated/other shapes? Give each study with DOI, the values compared, the direction and size of the effect, and whether only that variable changed. Prefer open-access papers.
answer:
## MoO₃-powder + sulfur-powder CVD: reported sulfur-supply comparisons

The clearest quantitative **sulfur-source-temperature** series is Wang *et al.*; the clearest **sulfur-source-position** series is Küçük *et al.* Neither supports a universal rule that more sulfur always makes larger monolayer triangles: both show a useful intermediate supply and less desirable products at the highest supply. Temperature is a heater setpoint, while position changes the sulfur source’s thermal environment; neither is a measured sulfur partial pressure at the substrate. (wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor pages 1-5, wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor pages 10-15, kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale pages 1-4, kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale pages 4-6)

| Study and DOI | Values compared and observed effect | Did only the stated sulfur variable change? |
|---|---|---|
| **Wang *et al.* (2025),** [10.1088/1361-648x/ae14c8](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-648x/ae14c8). MoO₃ and sulfur powders; separately heated sulfur source; SiO₂ with a photoresist-promoted region and an unpromoted region. | At sulfur-source setpoints **180, 200, 220, 250, 270, 300 °C**, the *promoted* region changed from ≈**3 µm rounded hexagons** at 180 °C, to soft-edged triangles at 200 °C, larger/straighter triangles at 220 °C, and well-defined triangles at 250 °C. At 270 °C it showed irregular, merging **0–30 µm** features and multilayer centres; at 300 °C, predominantly particles and submicrometre triangles. Across the temperature series, reported mean feature size rose from ≈**4 µm** at 180 °C to **9.8 µm** at 250 °C and **11.2 µm** at 270 °C, then fell to ≈**4 µm** at 300 °C. Promoted-region monolayer fraction peaked at **82%** and coverage at **18%**, both at 250 °C; monolayer fraction fell to **48%** at 300 °C. Unpromoted-region mean feature size remained **3–5 µm** and coverage **0.5–2%** across the series. The reported *population density* on the unpromoted side increased from **0.8 × 10³ to 3.1 × 10³ mm⁻²** between 180 and 200 °C, then was ≈**1.3 × 10³ mm⁻²** from 220 to 300 °C. It is a count of imaged particles/flakes, **not necessarily a density of MoS₂ nuclei**: the authors identify oxide particles on the unpromoted side. (wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor pages 1-5, wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor pages 10-15, wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor media 0c343ee9) | **For the reported temperature series, sulfur-source temperature was the intended varied parameter within each substrate type**; MoO₃/substrate temperature was reported as **835 °C**, sulfur loading **120 mg**, and N₂ flow **20 sccm**. Do **not** attribute the promoted-versus-unpromoted contrast to sulfur temperature: those areas also differ in promoter. At the separate **250 °C** matched-location promoter comparison, coverage was **15% versus 4%**, population density **1.0 × 10³ versus 2.4 × 10³ mm⁻²**, and the promoted large-flake size peak **14.4 µm** versus a **3.9 µm** unpromoted average. Those numbers quantify the **promoter effect at fixed sulfur temperature**, not a temperature effect; the paper separately reports 18% coverage at 250 °C in its temperature-series analysis. (wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor pages 1-5, wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor pages 5-10, wang2025enhancedchemicalvapor pages 10-15) |
| **Küçük, Çağlar & Turgut (2024), open-access *preprint*,** [10.21203/rs.3.rs-4502220/v1](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-4502220/v1). MoO₃ powder **with NaCl additive**, and sulfur powder. | Sulfur-source distance from furnace centre (**DSC**) was **18, 17.5, 17 cm**. From the paper’s **Fig. 6(d)**, approximate coverage by **<3-layer** material was **27%, 45%, 0%**, respectively; corresponding **≥3-layer** coverage was ≈**3%, 0%, 65%**. Thus moving the source **18 → 17.5 cm** increased thin-layer coverage by ≈**18 percentage points** (≈**1.7-fold**), whereas **17.5 → 17 cm** changed the dominant product to thicker, overlapping material rather than further improving monolayer coverage. The authors describe **17 cm** as sulfur-rich, giving unstable hexagonal-like/circular and overlapping multilayer flakes, and **17.5 cm** as the preferred position for large-area monolayer growth. They do **not** give a numerical domain-size or nuclei-density series for these three positions. (kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale pages 1-4, kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale pages 4-6, kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale media a906d2a7) | **Position is the stated variable in the Fig. 6 comparison**, but the accessible text does not explicitly document every other setting for each of those three runs; do not claim an exhaustively verified single-variable control. An **18 cm baseline** is specified as **680 °C, 12 min, 25 sccm Ar, 3 mg MoO₃/0.3 mg NaCl**. The paper also independently optimizes growth time, temperature, Ar flow and **boat design**. In particular, its **millimetre-scale continuous monolayer** result is attributed especially to an **open-ended quartz boat**; it is *not* the measured effect of moving the sulfur source by 0.5 cm. (kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale pages 1-4, kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale pages 4-6, kucuk2024lowcostmillimeterscale pages 6-12) |
| **Lara Saenz *et al.* (2016),** [10.1557/adv.2016.484](https://doi.org/10.1557/adv.2016.484). MoO₃ and sulfur powders. | Compared sulfur placements **36 versus 17 cm from furnace centre**. The **36 cm** run, assigned to an oxide-sulfurization route, yielded **rhomboidal crystals** with Raman evidence of **MoO₂ plus MoS₂** in some flakes and MoO₂ alone in others. The **17 cm** run, assigned to a vapor-phase reaction route, yielded **triangular, Raman-confirmed monolayer MoS₂**. No attributable fold-change in domain size, nucleation density, or coverage was reported. This is **not** a controlled triangle-versus-truncated-triangle comparison. (saenz2016effectsofsynthesis pages 4-6, saenz2016effectsofsynthesis media 0791ffe9) | **No.** The 36 cm condition was ramped at **15 °C min⁻¹** to 850 °C and held 15 min; the 17 cm condition used **17.6 °C min⁻¹** to 550 °C followed by **5 °C min⁻¹** to 850 °C and a 15 min hold. Both boat position and sulfur-arrival/thermal history changed. The paper cannot isolate position as the cause of the shape or phase difference. (saenz2016effectsofsynthesis pages 4-6) |

**Position guidance without an attributable comparison.** Shendokar *et al.* (2023), [10.3390/mi14091758](https://doi.org/10.3390/mi14091758), use MoO₃ and sulfur powders and describe placing sulfur roughly **15–18 cm upstream** of MoO₃, with **18 cm** reported for their setup. They say the position must be readjusted if the final temperature or ramp changes to maintain appropriate sulfur-vaporization timing. Although they report growth at **650 °C**, they do **not** supply matched 15-versus-18-cm domain-size, nucleation-density, coverage, or shape outcomes. It therefore supplies process context, **not an effect size or a sulfur-position-only experiment**. (shendokar2023towardslowtemperaturecvd pages 2-4, shendokar2023towardslowtemperaturecvd pages 5-7)

**Scope and interpretation.** The often-cited Senkić *et al.* sulfur-heater series, [10.1016/j.matchemphys.2022.127185](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matchemphys.2022.127185), does compare **135–145 °C** at fixed **50 sccm** in a morphology grid and reports more dendritic growth with increased sulfur temperature at lower growth temperatures. But its Mo feedstock is **drop-cast aqueous ammonium-heptamolybdate/sodium-molybdate**, *not vaporized MoO₃ powder*; it is therefore not another powder–powder result. Likewise, Song *et al.*’s open-access powder study, [10.26599/NR.2025.94907140](https://doi.org/10.26599/NR.2025.94907140), reports smooth **triangles plus truncated triangles** at a **580 °C MoO₃-source temperature** and regular triangles at **530 °C**, while explicitly holding its **sulfur source at 220 °C**. That shape change tests **Mo supply**, not sulfur-boat temperature or position. These distinctions matter when interpreting triangle-versus-truncated-shape claims as evidence about sulfur supply. (senkic2023effectsofcvd pages 5-10, senkic2023effectsofcvd pages 10-15, song2025synthesisofwaferscale pages 3-5)
